concepts.name: Exposure as light reaching sensor
concepts.summary: Explain that exposure is the amount of light recorded by the sensor and that images can be under-, over- or correctly exposed.

concepts.name: Aperture and f-numbers
concepts.summary: Describe aperture as the lens opening whose f-number is inversely related to its size and controls how much light enters.

concepts.name: Shutter speed and motion
concepts.summary: Explain that shutter speed sets how long the sensor is exposed, freezing motion when fast and blurring it when slow.

concepts.name: ISO sensitivity and noise
concepts.summary: Understand that ISO amplifies the sensor signal, brightening images at the cost of increased noise.

concepts.name: Autofocus and focus point
concepts.summary: Recall how to half-press the shutter to focus and place the focus point on the intended subject.

concepts.name: Rule of thirds
concepts.summary: Understand how placing subjects along thirds lines or intersections creates balanced framing.

concepts.name: Camera exposure modes
aliases: auto, P, A, S, M modes
concepts.summary: Identify what automatic, aperture priority, shutter priority and manual modes let the camera or photographer control.

misconceptions.text: A bigger f-number means a bigger lens opening.
More megapixels or a more expensive camera automatically produces better photos.
Raising ISO is free and has no effect on image quality.

concepts.name: Exposure triangle trade-offs
concepts.summary: Adjust aperture, shutter speed and ISO together to keep exposure constant while choosing the desired effect.

concepts.name: Depth of field control
concepts.summary: Use aperture, focal length and subject distance to make backgrounds sharp or blurred.

concepts.name: Reading the histogram
concepts.summary: Use the histogram to judge exposure and spot clipped highlights or shadows.

concepts.name: Exposure compensation
concepts.summary: Apply plus or minus compensation to correct the camera's metered exposure in bright or dark scenes.

concepts.name: White balance and color temperature
concepts.summary: Set white balance to match light sources so colors look natural or intentionally warm or cool.

concepts.name: Leading lines and framing
concepts.summary: Use lines, foreground elements and frames to direct the viewer's eye to the subject.

concepts.name: Hand-holding shutter speed guidelines
concepts.summary: Choose shutter speeds that avoid camera shake based on focal length and use stabilization or tripods when needed.

concepts.name: Basic RAW editing adjustments
concepts.summary: Apply crop, exposure, contrast and white balance adjustments to a RAW or JPEG file.

misconceptions.text: A correct exposure is whatever the camera meter says, so compensation is never needed.
A histogram bunched to one side always means a bad exposure.
Blurred backgrounds depend only on aperture and not on distance or focal length.

concepts.name: Metering modes and scene evaluation
concepts.summary: Choose a metering mode by analysing scene contrast and subject placement to predict how the camera will expose.

concepts.name: Dynamic range and highlight protection
concepts.summary: Analyse a scene's contrast against sensor limits and decide how to expose or bracket to retain detail.

concepts.name: Focus modes and tracking
concepts.summary: Match single, continuous and tracking autofocus to static or moving subjects and choose the focus area.

concepts.name: Direction and quality of light
concepts.summary: Analyse how light direction, size and diffusion shape texture, shadows and mood.

concepts.name: Compositional balance and visual weight
concepts.summary: Analyse how subject placement, contrast, color and negative space distribute visual weight.

concepts.name: Focal length and perspective
concepts.summary: Explain how focal length and shooting distance change perspective, compression and background relationships.

concepts.name: Selective editing and color adjustment
concepts.summary: Use masks, tone curves and color controls to refine specific areas while keeping the result natural.

concepts.name: Non-destructive editing workflow
concepts.summary: Organize, cull, edit non-destructively and export files appropriately for web or print.

misconceptions.text: Shooting in the golden hour is the only time good light exists.
Wide-angle and telephoto lenses differ only in how much they zoom, not in perspective.
Any exposure error can be fully fixed in editing.

concepts.name: Artificial and flash lighting
concepts.summary: Balance flash with ambient light using power, sync speed, modifiers and position to shape a subject.

concepts.name: Low-light and long-exposure technique
concepts.summary: Plan exposures for low light or motion blur using tripods, ND filters and noise trade-offs.

concepts.name: Anticipation and timing
concepts.summary: Evaluate a situation to predict peak action and choose when and how to capture it.

concepts.name: Color grading and tonal intent
concepts.summary: Evaluate color palettes and tone to support mood and refine grades deliberately.

concepts.name: Genre-specific technique adaptation
concepts.summary: Adapt exposure, focus, lens and approach to the demands of different genres.

concepts.name: Critique and image selection
concepts.summary: Evaluate images against intent and craft to select the strongest frames and diagnose weaknesses.

concepts.name: Visual storytelling and series
concepts.summary: Judge how images combine in a sequence to convey narrative, theme and consistency.

misconceptions.text: Flash always looks harsh and is only for dark scenes.
Rapid burst shooting replaces the need for anticipation.
A strong portfolio simply collects the best individual photos regardless of coherence.

concepts.name: Developing a personal visual style
concepts.summary: Synthesize subject choice, light, composition and processing into a recognizable, intentional style.

concepts.name: Concept-driven project design
concepts.summary: Design a multi-image project from a concept, planning methods, constraints and presentation.

concepts.name: Deliberate rule-breaking
concepts.summary: Judge when departing from conventions of exposure, focus or composition strengthens meaning.

concepts.name: Advanced lighting design
concepts.summary: Create custom lighting setups, combining natural and artificial sources, to realize a specific vision.

concepts.name: Ethics and context in photography
concepts.summary: Evaluate ethical issues of consent, representation and manipulation in making and presenting images.

concepts.name: Output, print and presentation
concepts.summary: Evaluate and choose output media, color management and sequencing for prints, books and screens.

concepts.name: Mentoring and critical analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse the work of others against historical and contemporary context to give constructive critique.

misconceptions.text: Style comes from applying a signature preset or filter to every photo.
Breaking the rules is always a sign of creativity regardless of whether it serves the image.
Photographs are objective records, so editing and framing choices carry no ethical weight.
